title: New on H-1B
ask: Do you have a Social Security number? Apply at a local SSA office with your passport, I-94 and I-797, at least 10 days after entry.
why: Payroll, banking, credit and your driver's licence all need it, and SSA can only find you once CBP's entry record has reached its systems.

title: New on H-1B
ask: Have you seen your Labor Condition Application (LCA) and the wage your employer promised on it?
why: Your employer must pay at least the LCA wage from your start date, cannot bench you without pay, and must give you a copy of the LCA on request.

title: Extension window is open
ask: Has your employer started your H-1B extension? It can be filed up to 6 months before your I-797 expires.
why: Filing early keeps you working under the 240-day rule if USCIS is slow and leaves time for premium processing or a request for evidence. H-4 family extensions (I-539) should go in at the same time.

title: Your I-797 date has passed
ask: Was your extension filed before the old I-797 expired, so the 240-day rule covers you? If the extension is approved, update the I-797 date in Me.
why: A timely filed extension lets you keep working for the same employer for up to 240 days past expiry. If nothing was filed, stop and talk to your employer or counsel today.

title: Six-year limit within a year
ask: Do you qualify to extend beyond six years: an approved I-140 with a priority date that is not current (3-year extensions), or a PERM or I-140 pending 365+ days (1-year extensions)? Have you counted days outside the US to recapture?
why: Without one of these, H-1B time ends at six years. Recaptured travel days and these extensions are what keep most Indian H-1B holders working while they wait.

title: Changing employer
ask: Has the new employer actually filed the H-1B petition (you have the receipt notice, or at least the courier confirmation) before your first day?
why: Portability lets you start when USCIS receives a non-frivolous petition, not when it is approved. Starting before filing is unauthorised work.

title: Changing employer
ask: Has your I-140 been approved for at least 180 days, so your priority date and extension eligibility travel with you even if the old employer withdraws it?
why: After 180 days an approved I-140 is not revoked just because the employer withdraws, and the priority date is yours for any future employment-based petition.

title: Changing employer
ask: Has your I-485 been pending 180+ days, and is the new job in the same or a similar occupation? If yes, file Supplement J.
why: Job portability keeps a pending green card alive when you change employers, but only with a same-or-similar role and a Supplement J on file.

title: Laid off
ask: Have you written down your last day of employment and counted 60 days from it (or until your I-94 expires, whichever comes first)?
why: Within the grace period a new employer can file for you, you can file a change of status (B-2, F-1, H-4), or you can leave. After it, you are out of status.

title: Laid off
ask: Did the employer offer to pay your reasonable return transportation home, and do you have your final pay and health-insurance continuation details?
why: An employer that ends an H-1B early must offer the cost of return transportation. It is also the moment to sort out COBRA and pending expense claims.

title: Travelling outside the US
ask: Have you confirmed with your employer or counsel that the September 2025 proclamation on H-1B entry (the $100,000 payment) does not apply to you before you travel?
why: USCIS guidance says it targets new petitions for workers outside the US, not extensions or existing visa holders, but the details and exceptions have changed more than once.

title: Your spouse
ask: Your I-140 is approved, so your spouse can apply for an H-4 EAD (Form I-765, category (c)(26)). Have they?
why: H-4 spouses of H-1B holders with an approved I-140 (or an extension beyond six years) may work. Many families wait years without realising they already qualify.

title: Child turning 21
ask: Have you planned for your child turning 21: a change to F-1 before the birthday, and a CSPA age calculation if an I-485 is or will be filed?
why: At 21 a child stops being an H-4 dependent and, unless the Child Status Protection Act protects them, drops out of your green-card case. The fix must be in place before the birthday.
